data.business: Avenue Supermarts Limited (DMart) is a national supermarket chain focusing on value-retailing across multiple product categories. The company primarily operates on a cash and carry business model along with sales to subsidiaries. It operates brick-and-mortar stores alongside the DMart Ready e-commerce platform and sells general merchandise and apparel largely consisting of private or pseudo-private labels.
data.narrative: The annual report and recent concalls align on DMart's physical retail store growth, reaching 500 stores and 20.58 million square feet of retail area while maintaining a cash and carry business model. However, management concalls place greater emphasis on the distinct operation of the DMart Ready e-commerce business, which runs at an EBITDA loss despite sales growth. Concalls also emphasize cost pressures not detailed in high-level annual report summaries, such as rising real estate prices, warehousing rental inflation, and wage increases that reduce return on capital.

bull.point: DMart expanded its footprint to 500 stores with 20.58 million square feet of retail area, operating successfully across states like Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Andhra Pradesh.
The company achieved a turnover close to INR 67,000 crores in the prior year while delivering 21% sales growth in its DMart Ready e-commerce business.
Credit risk from receivables remains insignificant, and the company has no history of loan defaults or being named a wilful defaulter.
The business passes vendor price drops directly to customers, generates volume surges during staple price deflation, and reduced employee attrition to 11.3%.

bear.point: The DMart Ready e-commerce operations run at an EBITDA loss of minus 2% to minus 3% with annual net losses of INR 247 crores, impacted by higher transportation costs for home deliveries.
Accelerated property purchases, higher per-location real estate prices, and rapid inflation in warehousing rentals and employee wages have hurt fixed asset turnover and lowered return on capital.
The company generated negative net cash flow used in investing activities of 4,206.96 Crores, leaving ending cash and cash equivalents at negative 96.56 Crores.

The defined benefit gratuity plan, carrying a 7-year weighted average obligation duration, exposes DMart to investment, interest rate, salary, mortality, concentration, and asset-liability matching risks.

data.balance: Net cash flow from operating activities for the year ended March 31, 2026 was 3,466.74 Crores, while net cash flow used in investing activities was 4,206.96 Crores. Short-term borrowings stood at 965.27 Crores as of March 31, 2026, with ending cash and cash equivalents net of bank overdrawn balances at negative 96.56 Crores.
